title: The half-standard-error rule for pooling within- and across-trial interactions
question: The published rule pools within-trial and across-trial interaction estimates when they differ by less than half the across-trial standard error. What are its pass rate, the bias and coverage of what it reports, and how does it compare with a test stated in the difference's own standard error?
design: Exact bivariate-normal computation over 24 network configurations (number of trials, dispersion of trial covariate means, ecological bias), with standard errors from a model of 200-patient trials and an individual-level check.
